newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says high interest rates temporary.
newsitem.headline: Manila says high interest rates temporary.

text.p: Philippine central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Tuesday the high interest rates were temporary and they would be brought down quickly as soon as the foreign exchange market stabilised.
"I can assure you as the situation stabilises, we will bring down the interest level very fast to normal levels," Singson said in an interview with a local television station.
The central bank has kept its overnight borrowing rate at a 2-1/2 year high of 32 percent since last Thursday, which prompted some big banks to raise their prime lending rates to over 30 percent.
"This (the high interest rates) is just temporary. This is just a question of time," Singson reiterated.
Singson said the central bank was auditing banks which may have violated the limits on dollar holdings. Banks are allowed to go long on dollars up to 20 percent of their capital.
"We are having the banks examined," he said.

Banks who may have exceed the limit would be fined 5,000 pesos a day for the first violation; their authority to open letters of credit would be suspended for the second violation; and the officer responsible for the first offense could be suspended for 90 days, Singson said.
